original_title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation Gets New Trailer at Gamescom 2026 Showing off Submarine Combat, Weapons, and More

en.title: Final Fantasy 7 Revelation: Submarine Combat and Weapons Revealed in New Trailer
en.summary: A brand new trailer for Final Fantasy 7 Revelation has dropped, showcasing intense submarine combat and the terrifying might of the iconic Weapons. Fans are buzzing with excitement over the glimpses of familiar threats and beloved characters.
en.body:
The highly anticipated **Final Fantasy 7 Revelation** treated fans to a spectacular new trailer during Gamescom's Opening Night Live, offering a substantial look at the game's escalating conflict. The footage prominently featured the game's most formidable antagonists: The Weapons. From Rufus Shinra's reassuring, yet perhaps naive, public service announcement on the Shinra News Network to the sheer destructive power unleashed upon Shinra soldiers, these colossal entities are clearly central to the unfolding narrative. The trailer didn't shy away from showcasing specific fan-favorite threats, with chilling glimpses of the **Ruby Weapon**, **Emerald Weapon**, and the imposing **Ultima Weapon**.

Beyond the existential threat posed by the planet's guardians, the trailer also delivered exciting gameplay reveals. We saw Tifa Lockhart donning a Black Mage class outfit, hinting at new character customization and combat roles. A stunning prerendered cutscene depicted the iconic airship, the Highwind, bravely confronting one of the Weapons. More intriguingly, the trailer provided an extended look at submarine gameplay. Players will apparently navigate the underwater depths in a submarine, with one sequence showing the party inside the vessel, the Huge Materia within reach, while dodging incoming attacks. This underwater combat section promises a fresh dimension to exploration and battle.

## Facing the Planet's Fury

The narrative weight of the trailer was amplified by key character dialogue. Vincent Valentine's voiceover cast a somber tone, explaining, "The Planet sees us as another threat to her well-being, and rightfully so." This sentiment was echoed by Cid Highwind, who declared, "You call 'em planetary warriors, but I call 'em weapons of mass destruction!" These lines underscore the complex relationship between humanity, the planet, and the Weapons, which are presented not just as boss encounters but as manifestations of the planet's desperate defense mechanisms. It remains to be seen if these Weapons will function as standard bosses or as optional super bosses, mirroring their roles in the original **Final Fantasy VII**. The trailer also included glimpses of classic exploration elements, such as the party parachuting from the Highwind, riding chocobos across the world map, and Yuffie Kisaragi exploring what appears to be her homeland, Wutai.

## Community Hype and Future Prospects

The reveal has sent waves of excitement through the **Final Fantasy** community. The inclusion of submarine combat and the detailed focus on the Weapons suggest a more expansive and lore-rich experience than many anticipated. Fans are particularly eager to learn more about how these legendary threats will be integrated into the gameplay and narrative. The trailer, while incredibly hype-inducing, unfortunately did not provide a specific release date. The current release window remains Spring 2027, with a simultaneous launch planned for PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series X|S.

## What's Next

With **Final Fantasy 7 Revelation** targeting a Spring 2027 release, expect further gameplay details and story revelations in the coming months. Keep an eye out for official announcements regarding the specific roles and challenges presented by the **Ruby Weapon**, **Emerald Weapon**, and **Ultima Weapon**, as well as more information on the expanded combat mechanics.

content_raw: Fans were treated to a new Final Fantasy 7 Revelation trailer at Gamescom’s Opening Night Live showcase, where we saw more of The Weapons, a submarine combat section, and more. The trailer opens up with Rufus Shinra sharing a public service announcement on the Shinra News Network regarding the looming Meteor and the Weapons, assuring citizens that humanity will “reign supreme” over these obstacles. We get to see one of these Weapons wreaking havoc on Shinra soldiers, as well as special shots of the Ruby Weapon, Emerald Weapon, and the Ultima Weapon. Gameplay footage showing Tifa wearing the Black Mage class outfit was is shown off, as well as a prerendered cutscene showing the Highwind facing off with a Weapon. We even get to see the inside of the submarine with the Huge Materia smack in the middle, along with an underwater combat section that shows the party navigating through the ocean as the submarine dodges attacks. Footage of the team parachuting down from the Highwind and riding chocobos through the world is also included, as well as Yuffie exploring what seems to be Wutai, making for an extremely hype trailer that is leaving fans more excited than ever. Most of the dialogue in the trailer centered around the Weapons, with Vincent Valentine explaining in a voiceover that "the Planet sees us as another threat to her well-being, and rightfully so." "You call 'em planetary warriors," Cid says. "But I call 'em weapons of mass destruction!" It remains to be seen if these featured Weapons will be normal bosses or super bosses, in keeping with the original game. Unfortunately, no specific release date was revealed, either. Spring 2027 is still the ongoing release window for the game, which will release simultaneously on PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (via Steam, Epic Games Store, and Xbox PC. This is the latest look we've gotten at FFVII Revelation following the trailers that were shown at Summer Game Fest earlier this year, where we were reintroduced to the Highwind. Using the airship, Cloud and company will be able to traverse all across the planet, dropping down via parachutes to explore to your heart's content. It also introduced the FITS system, which allows each character to change their playstyle based on Final Fantasy jobs. Speaking of gameplay, yes, you'll get the chance to play the gunslinging Vincent Valentine and even transform into the Galian Beast. As yet, not much else has been revealed about the game, but director Naoki Hamaguchi has publicly stated that he wants to integrate many of the Final Fantasy VII spin-off properties into its ultimate ending.
